summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, chronic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for cardiac optimization prior to a left below-the-knee amputation due to a chronic non-healing calcaneal ulcer. She underwent preoperative cardiac clearance with a P-MIBI stress test showing no ischemia. She continued her regular hemodialysis schedule and was started on vancomycin and ceftazidime for surgical prophylaxis. The amputation was performed without complications, and nerve catheters were placed for pain control, later replaced by a fentanyl patch. Mild incisional cellulitis developed postoperatively, managed with continued antibiotics. Due to a history of HIT and calciphylaxis, she was transitioned from warfarin to apixaban. Physical therapy recommended inpatient rehabilitation, and she was discharged to an extended care facility with plans to continue antibiotics with dialysis, wound monitoring, and follow-up with vascular surgery.
